label: Polyclinic
lead: Tier-2 polyclinics in Patna, Lucknow, Ranchi run on volume — 60+ patients before noon, half of them walk-ins, half on a queue token. The front desk holds it together. Lucoze gives them the tool that matches.
why: Walk-ins get inserted by triage code — emergency before fever before follow-up. Doctor knows what’s next.
Confirmation lands in Hindi. Reschedule is one tap. Fewer no-shows, week over week.
When Dr. Sharma is late, the queue rebalances to Dr. Reddy without a fight at the desk.
Cash, UPI, partial — one screen. End-of-day cash reconciliation in 5 minutes.

detail.title: A queue that survives 60 patients before noon
detail.body: A high-volume polyclinic runs on the front desk holding a moving queue together: walk-ins and token-holders, several doctors, everyone arriving at once. Lucoze inserts walk-ins by triage code — emergency before fever before follow-up — so the doctor always knows who is next. When a doctor runs late, the queue rebalances to another without an argument at the desk.

detail.title: Cash-first billing and same-day reconciliation
detail.body: Tier-2 OPD is a cash-and-UPI business with plenty of partial payments. Lucoze keeps cash, UPI and partial settlements on one screen and closes the day with a clean reconciliation, so the owner isn't rebuilding the day's takings from a drawer of receipts. Reminders and confirmations go out in Hindi over WhatsApp.

faqs.q: How does Lucoze handle walk-ins mixed with booked tokens?
faqs.a: Walk-ins are inserted into the live queue by triage priority alongside token-holders, so the doctor sees a single ordered list of who's next.

faqs.q: What happens when a doctor is delayed?
faqs.a: The queue rebalances to another available doctor, so patients aren't stranded and the front desk isn't negotiating the change by hand.

faqs.q: Does it support cash and UPI with partial payments?
faqs.a: Yes — cash, UPI and partial settlements are handled on one screen, with an end-of-day reconciliation that closes the books quickly.
